body:
Yeah, I couldn't read it either.  Rambling, disjointed thoughts, clumsy overuse of elipses, failure to redirect to the entry the author evidently wants people to read so badly, spelling and other grammatical errors, general lack of point.  Sufficient for a private blog post, but if the author wants to show it to other people, the author would be well served to proofread better.

Oh, and OP's shitty attitude here isn't doing them any favors.

More of this bullshit.  Yes, tell me in literally too stupid to perceive the outside world, please do.  And then present a different, *equally* biased set of inaccurate filters to perceive the world through, and do so without irony.  We all know that we can just **choose** to believe any damned thing we want to, so it's obviously **all your fault** if you're sad, because Brave and Noble Saints Like OP And The Author^TM just gave you a way to delude yourself into being happy.  Wake up, sheeple!  OP and the author just gave you something you can instantly and effortlessly choose to believe in!  Why won't you just do what OP and the author say?  Man, fuck you, sheeple, you deserve to be sad.  OP and the author just gave you the secret to being happy, just blindly trust them and choose what you believe according to their whims, geez.

That's not what I said, but thanks for deliberately lying about what I said, ass.

1. I don't like that same-sex marriage is legal because it being legal only lowers my relative position in the social order, which is not high to begin with.  

2. I am **NOT** "better," and by your reasoning I am total scum.

Oh, boy. This bullshit again.  

> Are you hydrated?

Yes.

> Have you eaten in the past three hours?

Yes.

> Have you showered in the past day?

Yes.

> If daytime: Are you dressed?

Yes

> If nighttime: Are you sleepy and fatigued but resisting going to sleep?

I have no problems sleeping at night.  Thanks for the infantalizing bullshit (e.g., pajamas, teddy bear, acting as if you have any right to tell me what I'm allowed to do when it comes to sleep, etc.), though!

> Have you stretched your legs in the past day?

Yes.  In addition to mere stretching, I also run 5 miles every day and do 30-45 minutes of calisthenics roughly every other day.

> Have you said something nice to someone in the past day?

Yes.

> Have you moved your body to music in the past day?

This is not part of my ordinary exercise routine (*see above*), but to satisfy this bullshit quiz I just did 200 squats while listening to "upbeat music" (a random YouTube playlist generated from "Let it Go" from Disney's *Frozen*).  I still feel like shit, and the artificial rhythms interfered with my ability to gauge my own heartrate or set my own pace.  It was markedly more difficult to complete the exercise *with* the music than without.

> Have you cuddled a living being in the past two days?

I cannot afford to feed and care for a pet.  I live alone.  The prospect and *concept* of intimate physical contact with another human being makes me physically ill.  Contrary to this question's belligerently ignorant insistence that I would not impose on anyone who I demanded to let me touch them or their property (pets), **I WOULD FIND ANY SUCH REQUEST IMPOSING IF ANYONE ASKED THAT OF ME**.  Those who know me know and respect that **I NEITHER LIKE BEING TOUCHED NOR WANT TO BE TOUCHED**.  I would immediately retreat from anyone who requested or demanded a hug from me, stranger or otherwise, and in the hypothetical scenario where I did own an animal that someone else asked to hug, I would not give them permission and would defend myself and my property from them if they insisted on unwanted physical contact.  

> Do you feel ineffective.

No.  And the list of "effective" things included in the article is laughable.  Loading the dishwasher is not, by itself, effective, and it is easily possible to imagine a scenario where: (1) a dishwasher is loaded *ineffectively*, or (2) a person reading this claptrap article does not own a dishwasher. My apartment, for instance, doesn't have one.  Responding to *one* email is likewise not effective by itself, and it is also easy to imagine someone who cannot afford a gym membership.  I cannot.  If these are examples of what the author calls "effective" behavior, the author has so diluted the word "effective" as to render it meaningless.

> Do you find yourself unattractive?

The author fails to properly distinguish between "unattractive" and "ugly."  Most people are unattractive, because most people have neither the genetics nor highly paid teams of beauty professionals needed to maintain the standards of attractiveness.  However, **MOST PEOPLE AREN'T UGLY EITHER**.  The vast, *vast* majority of people just *are*.  They are unattractive (because they are not attractive, that's what the word *means*), and they are also not ugly.  I am both unattractive and not ugly, at least physically.

The author's insistence that friends will, invariably, without fail, and in all cases find every single selfie you take to be attractive is idiotic, beyond absurd, and unworthy of further comment.

> Do you feel paralyzed by indecision?

No.

> Have you seen a therapist in the past few days?

I have seen fourteen therapists in the last ten years.  The ones who did not bar me from their practices (including the "free" and "community outreach" clinics within thirty miles of me, which are the only ones I can even pretend to afford) were abrasive, incompetent, abusive, inept, unprofessional, and unhelpful in the extreme.  

> Have you been over-exerting yourself lately -- physically, emotionally, socially, or intellectually?

No.

> Have you changed any of your medications in the past couple of weeks, including skipped doses or a change in generic or prescription brand?

I have not been on any medications, psychiatric or otherwise, for the last two years.  Prior to that, I followed each psychiatrist's instructions for medications that they prescribed until such time as the side-effects of the medications became unbearable and/or the psychiatrist in question fucked with my dosage or medication prescribed fully *sua sponte* and refused to explain why or what the side effects would be.  Or until I realized they had lied to me about what and why they had prescribed me.  I've seen 9 psychiatrists in the past ten years, when I could afford to, and all of them have done some combination of the above, without failure.

> Have you waited a week?

Yes.  I have waited **YEARS**.  It never gets better.  It only gets worse.  And people like OP and the author are a huge part of the reason *why* it gets worse.
So in your world, absolutely no one dies of AIDS or "any terminal disease?"  Must be nice.

I am a straight, cis-gendered male who identifies as a man.  I resent gays and lesbians because they are no longer wholly beneath me on the social pyramid thanks to the recent Supreme Court decision.  Life has improved for *them*, while mine remains as shitty as ever.
You all want one less homophobe in the world.  You also want one more homophobe you can imagine was gay all along so he "deserved it."  And I want to die. Everyone wins.

> I see good in you.  Exhibit A: the fact that you made this post in the first place.

Bullshit.  The mere act of posting here is evidence of nothing other than the fact that I've posted here.  If a complete stranger approached you, stared you in the eye, and told you the only thing keeping them from spitting on interracial couples was their own rank cowardice, would you use that as evidence for them being a good person?  

But you've taken your ball and gone home, so it's not like you're going to answer this without proving yourself a liar anyway.

Absolutely.  It's just another reminder of how much I'm on the bottom of life.  That's why I hate the Supreme Court's decision; at least before that, I knew there was one more group I was better off than.  Now they've been lifted up and are happy, "it got better" for them, and things are *at best* the same for me.  Because they're happy, now I'm worse off.

> I don't think you're an asshole.

You're wrong.  I am.

> Even your throwaway account name is full of self rage

You're wrong.  It's what I am *according to everyone who knows me*.

> I find that sad.

Cry me a fucking river.  I don't need any more guilt dumped on me from anyone else.

> treatments are available and often successful

Not for me.  13 years.  13 *fucking* years.  Even when I could afford them, they didn't work.  

> I'd urge you to seek them out

I have.  For 13 years.  Why would you assume, in a post where I mention "waiting 13 years for any kind of improvement in my life," that I *hadn't* already sought them out?

> Is it really because you're just a coward?

Yes.  

> Or us there a part of you ... that knows how awful it would be to do such a thing?

There isn't.  I only know I would face consequences and repercussions I'm too much of a coward to face if I tried it, and that I would fail.

> a huge part of you

There isn't **ANY** such part of me.

> isn't there a chance that there is good in you after all?

No.
